title: A customer card: create, save and find it again
goal: Create a training customer, find the saved card, rename it and distinguish its name, code and identity.

prerequisites.text: Use your service from the previous lesson with Customers/Services/Requests commands. If they are absent, complete the previous preparation. No programming or coded reference handling is required.

sections.title: Why keep a customer record
paragraphs: The same customer may return to the workshop. Re-entering a name from memory can produce inconsistent spellings and lose the relationship between visits. The Customers catalog keeps customer records separately from future requests. A card is the window for one record. Today a fictional name is enough; no phone, address or personal information is needed.

A field is a place for one value in a card. Наименование is the human-readable customer name. This configuration assigns a code automatically when saving. Do not invent a code in advance or expect your code to equal a screenshot’s number.

sections.title: From an empty form to a saved row
paragraphs: In Enterprise mode open Customers and clear search. Choose Create. Enter Учебный Север in Наименование and leave the code automatic. Choose Save and close. Find the row again and reopen it by double-click or the normal open command. This checks persistence, rather than merely text that was typed.

The example shows the sequence and expected observation. Merely reading it does not create a customer in your base. The independent task uses different fictional names. Do not copy somebody else’s result into your self-report as evidence.

code.source: Клиенты → Создать → Наименование: Учебный Север → Записать и закрыть → найти → открыть
code.output: The reopened card shows Учебный Север and its automatically assigned code.

sections.title: Typed does not mean saved
paragraphs: Before saving, the text may exist only in the open form. Closing and discarding changes is not saving. Our criterion therefore has two actions: save, then reopen the found row. If you forgot to save, return to the form and use its save action; do not create repeated copies through Create.

Search helps find rows by text. If a saved row is invisible, clear the earlier query, refresh the list and verify the base. Search does not delete records; it can temporarily hide nonmatching rows. One filtered list is not proof that a customer disappeared.

sections.title: Rename a record or create another customer
paragraphs: Reopen the earlier card and change only its name to Учебный Север — сервис. Save and reopen. Its code remains the one you observed before renaming: the same record now has a new label. Creating another customer through Create is a different action. Identical names alone do not prove identical records.

A record has its own identity; 1C applications refer to it through a reference. The essential meaning is that a request selects a particular customer, not just similar text. No UUID study or BSL is required here. The code in this catalog and reopening help you navigate; a code is not globally unique across every infobase.

sections.title: Two new customers for your service
paragraphs: Create Учебный Восток, save it and find it again. Note its actual code. Rename that same card to Учебный Восток — сервис. Then use Create separately for Учебный Запад. With search cleared, both records must be available; any example records you created remain as well.

Compare the results: East has a new label with its earlier code; West has a separate card. Explain why a future request cannot reliably choose a customer merely by a similar name. The next lesson uses your East record, so preserve your work rather than clearing the list.

practice.title: On your own: East and West
practice.task: Create Учебный Восток, save and reopen it. Rename that same card to Учебный Восток — сервис. Separately create Учебный Запад. Find and open both, comparing their actual codes while preserving earlier example records.
practice.environment: Official installed 1C in a separate training infobase. Nexus shows the lesson and keeps an optional draft; it does not run this program.
practice.externalRoute: Follow the steps labelled by application. The self-report field records your external observation; it is not Nexus verification.

passport.goal: Save, find, rename and distinguish two records.
passport.start: Your service from the previous lesson; existing records remain.
passport.knowledge: List, card, field, save and search are explained above.
passport.change: Names of your new fictional customers; codes are automatic.
passport.result: Renamed East with its earlier code, and a separate West.
passport.checks: Reopen both rows and keep your observation record.
passport.errors: Closing without saving, an old search, or creating instead of renaming.
passport.recovery: Discard an unsaved form edit and find the earlier record. Do not delete the base or earlier customers.

steps.action: Create and save East; reopen it and record its actual code.
steps.why: So the action has an observable, reproducible result.

steps.action: Rename East, then create West separately. Clear search and open both cards.
steps.why: So the action has an observable, reproducible result.
steps.expected: Two distinct records and one changed label.

cases.label: After returning
cases.input: Open East and West from the list.
cases.output: East — service retains its previously observed code; West is separate. Your actual codes can differ from examples.

criteria: Renaming was performed in the existing card.
Earlier records are preserved; real personal data was not used.
practice.hint: To rename, open the found row; Create begins a different customer.

referenceSolution.source: Example comparison: East was created, saved and reopened. Record its actual code in your own notes. Renaming that card produces Учебный Восток — сервис with its earlier code. West is created separately with its own card and code. A name is a label; record identity remains. Both rows are available after clearing search, and earlier customers remain. Use codes from your base, not from this reference.
paragraphs: A reference for reasoning and expected observation. It neither fills your record nor certifies completion.

selfcheck.prompt: How do you check that an entered customer was actually saved?
options: Look at text in an unsaved form
Save, find the row and reopen it

selfcheck.prompt: Renaming the existing card necessarily creates another customer?
options: No, it can be the same record with a new label
selfcheck.feedback: Creating another record differs from changing its name.

selfcheck.prompt: After saving, a row is invisible under an earlier search. What is a safe first action?
options: Clear search and verify the base
selfcheck.feedback: Filtering can hide an existing row.

selfcheck.prompt: Your code differs from an example. Is that necessarily wrong?
options: No: record the actual automatically assigned code
selfcheck.feedback: Observe identification rather than guessing a number.

selfcheck.prompt: What does Create do instead of reopening East?
selfcheck.feedback: Open an existing card to rename it.

selfcheck.prompt: Explain name, observed code and customer identity using your rename and separate creation.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare your explanation with the walkthrough; it is not graded automatically.
